title: Lakes of molten lava are so rare that only eight were reported in 2019
body: Erta Ale, whose name means “smoking mountain” in the local Afar language, rises 613 m from Ethiopia’s Danakil Depression, a region below sea level where three tectonic plates are splitting apart. Its summit holds one or sometimes two active lakes of molten rock that occasionally overflow, and one has been reported since at least 1906, the longest-existing lava lake known. Volcanoes with lava lakes are rare: in 2019 only **eight** were reported anywhere in the world. Watch the lake’s skin in the clip: it cools into a dark crust that keeps tearing open along glowing cracks.

slides.text: That makes it the longest-existing lava lake known. The summit sometimes holds two lakes at once, and they occasionally overflow down the volcano’s south side.

slides.prompt: Erta Ale stands where something unusual is happening to the ground beneath it. What?
slides.answer: Three tectonic plates are splitting apart
slides.detail: It sits at the Afar triple junction, near the southern end of the Red Sea Rift, in a depression that lies below sea level.

slides.question: What does the name Erta Ale mean in the local Afar language?
slides.explanation: Erta Ale means “smoking mountain”, a fitting name for a volcano whose summit lava lake is wreathed in fumes, as in the clip.
